questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Opportunity to live in a dorm close to my campus as well as a station to make it easier to travel by public transportation. 
That the study destination/city I chose would not be as crowded as Tokyo.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was lots of paperwork to fill out while in Japan.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy enough. We got sent lots of information over e-mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got some papers with information when we got our dorm room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Two dormitories close to the Fukakusa Campus (approx. a 5-7 minute walk): Mitra-kan and International House. 

Rooms in Mitra-kan have their own private toilets.
There are single or twin-rooms available at International House. First and second floor are unisex, third floor is female-only. 

I was planning on applying for a room at Mitra-kan, but we were sent the dorm application link two days before the deadline, with only rooms left at International House. I'm not sure whether Ryukoku University or UCPH forgot to send us the link, or whether there was miscommunication between the two, but being sent the dorm application so late was a big stressor. I was lucky to get one of the last single rooms, but I find it very odd that before we could even apply for a spot at Ryukoku University, UCPH sent us a mail regarding housing wishes (whether we'd like to move in to one of their dorms or if we'd like to find our own housing) and yet we got to apply for the dorms right before the deadline.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
There are kitchens on the second and third floor at International House. The kitchens have shared fridges and shelving units. If you want/need more storage, you can request to use/have one of the many drawers as well. 

I don't know about Mitra-kan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Since you'll be living with people from different cultures, you can't really have the same expectations regarding e.g. hygiene as you do for yourself. 
In our dorm groupchat there'd frequently be sent pictures or texts regarding how disgusting states bathrooms and kitchen were left in. 
A girl on the third floor slipped on some oil someone had left on the kitchen floor, and injured her knee pretty badly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The kitchens were often left dirty and smelly. Even though there were cleaners almost daily, the toilets were also left extremely disgusting even with all the notices and posters around (remember to wash your hands, remember to leave the toilet clean, etc.)
In the mens bathrooms there was often pee on the ground. In the womens bathroom there was left feces and sometimes period blood on the seats. 

Could just be the students this semester though.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to download excel-sheets and cross off the courses we'd like to register for, and then upload said sheet. It was rather easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
There is a website where you can look up the syllabus for each class.
You could ask R-Globe.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes I applied for. I was however adjusted down from JEP-3 to JEP-2, as the teachers assessed I wasn't academically fit for the higher level.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read each syllabus

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The Japanese classes were level-appropriate but very oral-oriented. We'd often do short presentations and sit and talk in groups. 

Japanese Pop Culture was kind of interesting, but the workload was slightly heavy. Lots of readings each weak with questions to answer. Two presentations and a final paper. 
Our professor in Japanese Media and arts made the course very interesting even with all the weekly readings/watchings and questions. A final paper and a presentation. 
We didn't have any homework in Japanese Religions B. We went on a few trips and did a presentation on our final paper. It wasn't as demanding as the other courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The loads of presentations and conversations in the Japanese classes were rather challenging as we haven't practiced that much conversation at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Japanese language 'package' (taught in Japanese): JEP-2 Core, Listening, Reading, Homeroom
Electives taught in English: Japanese Pop Culture, Japanese Religions B, Japanese Media and Arts

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Japanese Media and Arts. It was really interesting.

questions.answer: I don't think I had any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transportation was so much cheaper than in Denmark. 
I probably spent around 50dkk monthly because of class trips, but in my free time I spent more. It was still very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I once saw a poster at our dorm that advertised free karate lessons.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Our dorm went on a one-day trip to Amanohashidate and a temple. We went by bus and only paid 1000yen. I think it was a nice experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to shrines, temples or museums. Go on walks and enjoy the nature in Japan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy enough. There wasn't much to adjust to I think

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't remember any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Before the semester started, R-Globe helped (those of us who wanted) requesting special aid. I struggle with presentations, especially in front of large groups, so I asked to instead do them only in front of the teacher or smaller groups. We spent 1 hour+ writing the request, yet nothing happened. I wasn't even told it got outright rejected. 
However most of my course professors were understanding and accommodating, so I recommend you just talk directly with your professors rather than spend time with R-Globe and Karen on something that's really just for formality's sake.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing living in Japan. Seeing its beautiful nature, especially lots of mountains.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Courses with lots of presentations and all the paperwork to fill out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
